issues.description: SigningMode-to-bytes mapping is duplicated between sign_message and verify_signature in signing.py.
issues.detail: Both functions reimplement the SigningMode to message-bytes transform with parallel if/elif ladders and subtly different defaults. Extract one pure helper message_bytes(mode, message) -> bytes used by both, so the CHIP-0002 prefix-hashing rule lives in exactly one place.

issues.description: verify_signature leaks the RPC response type VerifySignatureResponse into the util layer.
issues.detail: chia/wallet/util/signing.py imports and returns VerifySignatureResponse from wallet_request_types, coupling the reusable signing library to the RPC wire schema. Return a small (bool, str | None) result or a dedicated struct local to signing.py so non-RPC callers can reuse the function, which was the stated motivation for extraction.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum decision table is incomplete and falls through implicitly to CHIP_0002.
issues.detail: The free function enumerates three of four (is_hex, safe_mode) combinations explicitly and lets the fourth land on a default return. Make the mapping total via an explicit dict keyed by the tuple or a match with all four arms stated, so the truth table is readable and a future flag cannot silently land in the default.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic lives on Wallet but uses no instance state and is called via main_wallet for unrelated DID/NFT keys.
issues.detail: The method only calls calculate_synthetic_secret_key with a module constant and is reached through self.service.wallet_state_manager.main_wallet for DID and NFT flows where main_wallet identity is irrelevant. Move it to a module-level function in chia/wallet/util/signing.py to remove the wrong-boundary placement.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum exists as both a free module function and a @property that just delegates to it.
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py defines signing_mode_enum as a function and also adds an identically named property on two request classes that calls the function. Pick one location: either keep the property holding the logic or have callers use the function directly, so there is one name for one behavior.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring still references a removed `request` parameter.
issues.detail: The extracted free function takes signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, and address as keyword arguments, but the docstring carries over `:param request:` from the prior RPC method. Rewrite the docstring to match the new signature; the staleness signals that the contract for the freshly extracted utility was not written down.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the extraction of sign_message/verify_signature into chia/wallet/util/signing.py is the right direction, collapsing three near-duplicate per-wallet implementations into one library function. The remaining concerns are consistent across reviewers: the SigningMode-to-bytes transform is duplicated inside signing.py, the (is_hex, safe_mode) truth table is incomplete and split between a free function and a property, the new util leaks the RPC response type VerifySignatureResponse, and convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is misplaced on Wallet despite using no instance state. None of these block merge, but the cleanup is cheap and would make the new boundary actually clean.
